title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
Udio, an AI music generator, was deployed to create original songs from text prompts. The system was trained on copyrighted music without authorization, generating songs similar to existing hits. The failure occurred at the training stage, where copyrighted works entered the model's training data without licensing agreements or artist compensation in place.

What would have caught this: licensing agreements negotiated before training began, or audit mechanisms to verify that training data came only from authorized sources. Instead, Udio operated the system and released it to users before securing rights to the music it had learned from. Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group later settled with Udio and agreed to build a licensed platform. Sony Music has filed separate lawsuits alleging over 30,000 copyrighted recordings were used to train the system.

It is not established whether this training occurred with knowledge that the data was unauthorized, or what technical safeguards, if any, were considered during development.

summary:
Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, which had been accused of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system. Under the settlement, Udio has agreed to launch a new platform next year that will only use authorized and licensed music. The company will also allow users to customize, stream, and share music while compensating artists who opt into the platform. UMG's CEO stated the agreements demonstrate the company's commitment to supporting artists while embracing new technologies and developing innovative business models.

Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees, creates original music from text prompts using AI. The original lawsuit alleged that Udio had used hits like The Temptations' "My Girl" to generate similar songs without permission or compensation. This marks Udio's first major licensing agreement with a major music label. Financial terms were not disclosed. On the same day, UMG also announced a partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists, producers, and songwriters.
